recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is; no core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-7053 unless a future work group decision changes the Flag versus DetectedIssue boundary.
issue_request: FHIR-7053 was a Published Patient Care change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking what recommended approach should be used for recording alerts after AllergyIntolerance said it was not for alerts. The approved resolution was to append that alerts are handled using Flag or, where event-specific, Contraindication.
initial_application: Commit a30496dcda9c86251cf286f1636c23e570a80113 explicitly listed #7053 and changed the AllergyIntolerance alert misuse bullet to point to Flag or event-specific Contraindication. Commit cc54b56e72272bed97b5c33459fc90bc2bfe52d8 later replaced Contraindication with DetectedIssue in the same sentence.
additional_context: AllergyIntolerance is active in source/fhir.ini, and current source/allergyintolerance/allergyintolerance-introduction.xml says alerts are handled using Flag or event-specific DetectedIssue. source/fhir.ini records that Contraindication became DetectedIssue. FHIR-32856 later quoted the same Misuse section during Patient Care review, and Flag documentation remains consistent with using Flag for condensed alerting information and DetectedIssue for planned or ongoing action-related issues.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope source preserves the FHIR-7053 guidance with the current resource name DetectedIssue replacing the historical Contraindication reference.
